Photograph: Stefanie Keenan/Getty Images for Academy Museum of Motion Pictures Law Russell Brand accuser Mia Latter waives anonymity to call for consent law change Mia Latter says she was in an abusive relationship with the convicted rapist when he was 30 and she was 16 Raphael Boyd and Mark Brown Sun 15 Nov 2026 04.58 EST First published on Sat 14 Nov 2026 19.17 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A woman who alleges she was raped by Russell Brand when she was 16 has waived her right to anonymity to campaign for a staggered age of consent. Mia Latter says she was in an abusive three-month relationship with Brand when he was 30 and she was 16. Previously identified using the pseudonym “Alice”, Latter said in an interview with the Sunday Times that she had been inspired by Gisèle Pelicot to give up her lifelong right to anonymity. “It’s not my shame,” she said. “It’s not my burden to carry any more. It’s not me lying, and I didn’t commit any crimes.” Latter is calling on the UK government to introduce a “staggered” consent law, which would make it illegal for adults over a certain age to have sex with 16- and 17-year-olds.

pages.text: Russia barred from Junior Ice Hockey World Championships in Canada - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022 By Dan Roan Sports editor Published 15 November 2026 Russia's hopes of reintegration into international sport suffered a setback when it was barred from the upcoming Junior Ice Hockey World Championships in Canada. It comes despite a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) last month ordering the country's return to the competition. The hosts then said they would deny entry to Russian athletes as a result of the war in Ukraine. "Due to the position and restrictions formally communicated by the Canadian government, the Russian Under-20 national team is unable to participate in the World Junior Championship," the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) said in a statement. It added that "after carefully assessing the feasibility of alternative arrangements, the IIHF Council has determined that Canada will remain as host and the tournament will proceed from 26 December 2026 to 5 January 2027 in Edmonton and Red Deer." The Russian Ice Hockey Federation called the IIHF's decision "unacceptable and unlawful" and said it would appeal to the International Olympic Committee (IOC). "The IIHF's decision was made solely due to political reasons," it added. Photograph: Vasily Fedosenko/Reuters Fossil fuels Russia, Saudi Arabia and Australia named as biggest CO2 exporters in history Analysis of fossil fuel exports since 1850 differs from most assessments – which look at countries where CO 2 is released Fiona Harvey and Simon Evans in Antalya Tue 17 Nov 2026 00.00 EST Last modified on Wed 18 Nov 2026 00.08 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Russia, Saudi Arabia and Australia are the three biggest exporters of carbon dioxide in history, according to analysis of fossil fuels since 1850. Russia tops the list of global exporters of fossil fuels, with its vast coal, oil and gas deposits. Accounting for the CO 2 produced by burning these exports, Russia has been responsible for almost 70 gigatonnes, up to the end of 2025. He sets the strategic direction for the Office and administers its Global Energy Security and Strategic Petroleum Reserve programs, including the associated analysis, budget, and natural gas regulation efforts. United States Department of Transportation In This Section Safety Management System (SMS) What is a Safety Management System ( SMS )? SMS is the formal, top-down, organization-wide approach to managing safety risk and assuring the effectiveness of safety risk controls. It includes systematic procedures, practices, and policies for the management of safety risk. An international best practice for the management of system safety, SMS provides a means for a structured, repeatable, systematic approach to proactively identify hazards and manage safety risk. By incorporating SMS, aviation organizations are better able to proactively develop and implement mitigations that are appropriate to their specific environment and operations. The FAA uses SMS across the entire agency to ensure that the United States fulfills our International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) requirements for a State Safety Program (SSP). The FAA also uses SMS to actively manage the safety of air navigation services provided by the FAA throughout the United States. Then He Was Imprisoned Over Owning a Book After buying his own liberty, the Marylander covertly assisted conductors on the Underground Railroad, including Harriet Tubman. But his possession of “Uncle Tom’s Cabin” turned him into an abolitionist hero Green, from an illustration published in 1872 Wood Etching from William Still’s 1872 book “The Underground Railroad” Wikimedia Green, from an illustration published in 1872 Wood Etching from William Still’s 1872 book “The Underground Railroad” Wikimedia The knock on Samuel Green’s door must have felt inevitable. It was April 1857, and in the past decade hundreds of Black Marylanders had slipped off the farms and plantations where they were enslaved. Now local white leaders were beginning to suspect that Green knew more about the runaways than he let on. Green was a free Black man who lived in a cottage in Dorchester County, on the Eastern Shore of the Chesapeake Bay, where he farmed a modest plot and preached the word of God. pages.text: Santander, Spain: A 2027 Guide to Its Waterfront Art Museums | National Geographic TRAVEL BEST OF THE WORLD Beloved by Spaniards, Santander Is Becoming a Global Art Mecca The easygoing beachfront city is getting a host of new and reborn museums. A 2014 transformation by landscape architect Fernando Caruncho more than doubled the size of Pereda Gardens, in the historic heart of Santander. Luis Fonseca, Getty Images By Eddi Fiegel Published October 20, 2026 Santander, a port city in northwestern Spain, has long seduced Spaniards with its spectacular horseshoe bay surrounded by rolling green hills and the Cantabrian mountains in the distance. But now the city, the capital of the Cantabria region, is poised to become an international art destination. In September 2026, the new arts, culture, and technology center Faro Santander opened in a historic building redesigned by acclaimed British architect David Chipperfield with a permanent collection including works by such legendary figures as el Greco, Rubens, Velázquez, and Goya. ( See all 25 of the destinations that made our list of the best places to visit in 2027. ) Meanwhile, 2027 will bring the first outpost of Madrid’s renowned Reina Sofía museum. The impressive Museum of Prehistory and Archaeology of Cantabria also has a new home designed by the Barcelona-based architecture practice Mendoza Partida. Art lovers are sure to appreciate the city’s walkable city center—where ornate, neoclassical façades sit alongside Baroque churches and grand, porticoed squares—and the wide sandy beaches lined with elegant fin-de-siècle villas.

pages.text: Sarina Wiegman contract: Why England manager faces biggest challenge yet - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Sarina Wiegman has won the past three Women's European Championships - with the Netherlands in 2017 and England in 2022 and 2025 By Joe Bradshaw BBC Sport senior journalist Published 19 October 2026 When Sarina Wiegman took the reins as England manager in September 2021, she declared she had "come to bring the next level". Winner of the 2017 Women's Euros with her own Netherlands and runner-up at the subsequent World Cup in 2019, she certainly had the pedigree, but could she deliver on her promises? Five years on, Wiegman has pocketed two more European Championships and acquired another silver medal on the global stage. Not only that, but the success of her Lionesses exploded the women's game in this country, taking it not just to a new level, but to previously unthinkable heights. And yet on the day Wiegman extends her deal until after the Euros in 2029, her newest challenge could be her hardest yet. England manager Wiegman signs contract extension Published 19 October Why must England evolve? Wiegman's successful England teams have been built on a core group of players from an outstanding generation - but a few cracks have appeared this year. Seven of the team that started against world champions Spain in June also played in the Euro 2022 final against Germany - and their 4-0 defeat in Mallorca laid bare the gap England must bridge to the world's best. That result also consigned England to two rounds of play-offs to reach next summer's World Cup.
